brand_notes.photoSet: Local folder assets/products/outer-shell-adventure/ holds 23 files, all named 'specs-*'. These are NOT line-art diagrams - they are real studio product photographs with dimension lines overlaid directly on the photo (maker's own marketing/spec graphics), so hardware, panel colour-blocking and stitching are directly visible and usable as photographic evidence, not just numbers. Two products (Oval Dry Bag 5L and 10L) have no local file at all - that gap was filled by fetching the maker's live product page images (see that product's evidence).
brand_notes.colorBlocking: Outer Shell's 'bold two-tone' identity is real but concentrated in specific lines, not universal. The Bar Bag / Stem Caddy / Mega Bar Bag family is the clearest example: a solid main-colour body (tan, maroon, olive) with a CONTRASTING BLACK roll-top or drawcord collar sewn on above it - e.g. Mega Bar Bag is coyote-tan body with a black roll-top collar (specs-mega-bar-bag-2.png), Stem Caddy is maroon body with a black drawcord collar (specs-stem-caddy.png). The Seatpack / Saddlebag / Half Frame Bag / Top Tube Bag families are NOT two-tone panel-blocked - they are one dominant fabric (often a MultiCam-style camo print sold as the 'Black' colourway) trimmed only with black webbing straps and a small tan 'OUTER SHELL' woven label. Do not render the whole catalogue as two-tone; apply the contrast-collar split only to the products noted below.
brand_notes.cameoColourway: Several photographed samples use a camo/MultiCam print for what brands.json lists as the 'Black' colourway (hex #1c1c1c) - e.g. both Seatpacks (specs-seatpack-1/2.png) are shown in a dark black-multicam print, not a flat solid black. A flat #1c1c1c fill is the correct fallback (pattern fill is out of scope) but is worth knowing it will read flatter than the real product.
brand_notes.basketDependent: Per HANDOVER.md's basket-tracking list, TWO products in this catalogue need a Wald 137-style front basket rather than the bare rack the renderer draws: '137 Basket Bag' (named for the Wald 137 basket it's built to sit inside - explicit in the maker copy) and 'Rack Bag' (19L). The Rack Bag's own maker copy only says it fits 'small racks (Wald 1372, Pelago, Velo Orange)', which reads more like small platform/porteur racks than a wire basket, so this flag is carried forward from HANDOVER's determination rather than independently re-derived here - flagging the ambiguity rather than silently dropping it. Both are marked fits:'basket' below.
brand_notes.oualDryBagOrigin: The Oval Dry Bag product page's own photos (fetched live, not in the local folder) show a bag branded 'SealLine' - a Cascade Designs dry-bag brand, not Outer Shell's own house label. This is very likely a real OEM relationship (Outer Shell selling a rebranded/sourced SealLine roll-top dry bag as the payload for their Handlebar Harness) rather than a scraping error, since it appears consistently across the product's hero and detail shots including an on-bike lifestyle photo. Treated as legitimate supporting evidence for hardware/closure type (roll-top + side-release buckle, PurgeAir valve on the translucent version) but NOT for Outer Shell house colourways/branding - noted per-product.

products.name: Seatpack
products.dims_raw: Maker spec photo (specs-seatpack-1.png): length 16.5"-20" (range), height 6" (single figure, not a range), plus a 1.5" tab label near the compression buckle that is a strap-loop width, not the bag's own width. On-bike photo (specs-seatpack-2.png) shows 6.5" saddle-to-tire clearance and 2" of exposed seatpost required.
products.dims_note: len is the UNFURLED max of the range (20in=50.8cm) per the dimension rule. hgt is NOT a range in this product - the maker gives one figure only (6in=15.2cm) because the bag has a rigid arch-shaped internal frame (per brands.json feature note) that holds height constant; what the roll-top actually adjusts is reach/length at the tail, not height. So the usual 'roll shortens height' logic does not apply here and no render override is needed (height is effectively fixed - see render note below). wid (across the body) is not shown in either local photo; carried forward unverified from the prior catalogue figure of 21.6cm - flagged rather than guessed. Volume check with wid unverified: 50.8x21.6x15.2=16681cc=16.7L vs stated 10.5L, ratio 1.59 - a normal wedge ratio, so the carried-forward width is at least plausible.

geometry.notes: Squared nose clamped at the saddle rails/seatpost, tapering to a rounded tail that rolls closed. Internal arch frame keeps the cross-section from collapsing, so unlike most seatpacks this one does not visibly sag or narrow much between full and light packing.

closure.hardware: single wide black webbing strap with a side-release buckle, doubling as the compression strap

details.seams: sewn, black webbing binding at the tail edge
details.fabric: 1000D Cordura PU or EPLX600 ECOPAK; photographed sample is a dark black/olive MultiCam-style camo print, not flat black, though brands.json lists it under the 'Black' colourway

mount.notes: Maker-stated fit requirement: minimum 2in exposed seatpost and 6.5in saddle-to-tire clearance (165mm) for this size; clearance_tyre_mm reflects that maker figure rather than a generic default.

products.name: Seatpack

details.seams: sewn, black webbing binding at the tail edge

mount.notes: Maker-stated fit requirement: minimum 4.5in exposed seatpost and 8in saddle-to-tire clearance (203mm) for this size.

products.name: Rolltop Saddlebag
products.dims_raw: Maker spec photo: 11in height (single figure, no range given), 3in x 4in base.
products.dims_note: The maker's assembly diagram (specs-rolltop-saddlebag-2.webp: 'Roll! Clip! ... Attach seatpost strap!') shows this mounts the SAME way as the full Seatpack - nose clipped to the saddle rails via a 3-prong strap, tail rolls closed and points backward, seatpost strap for stability. So the 11in figure is the bag's own LENGTH (nose-to-tail, the roll axis) not its height, matching the original catalogue assignment: len=11in=27.9cm, wid/hgt=4in/3in=10.2/7.6cm (fixed cross-section, no taper visible). Only one length figure is published (no min/max range), so it is used as-is per the single-figure rule. Volume check: 27.9x10.2x7.6=2163cc=2.16L against the stated MAX capacity of 2.1L, ratio 1.03 - an almost exact match, confirming 11in is the near-max-volume unfurled state rather than an arbitrary figure.

geometry.notes: Small rectangular box, minimal taper visible in the studio photo; reads as a scaled-down Seatpack rather than a wedge.

closure.hardware: single side-release buckle, tan/khaki webbing roll-top tape contrasting with the orange body

details.reflective: small reflective strip on the tail-side seam (visible in specs-rolltop-saddlebag.png)
details.fabric: photographed sample is a solid burnt-orange body with a contrasting tan/khaki roll-top collar and black webbing/buckle - one of the more clearly two-tone products in the catalogue

mount.notes: Small under-saddle stash pouch, no maker-stated clearance figure found (unlike the two Seatpacks); no clearance evidence beyond the general small-bag assumption.

products.name: Half Frame Bag
products.dims_raw: Maker spec photo 'SMALL HALF FRAME BAG': top rail 17in, main body height 4.25in (dashed centre measurement), front strap-tab height 2in, a further diagonal tail-taper run of 5.5in.
products.dims_note: len (17in=43.2cm, top rail) and hgt (4.25in=10.8cm, main body height at the zip line) both confirmed by photo and match the prior catalogue exactly. wid (depth off the frame) is NOT visible in this side-elevation photo and is carried forward unverified from the prior 5.7cm estimate - flagged rather than guessed. Considered reading the 5.5in diagonal figure as width/depth instead, but rejected: it stays roughly constant (5.5/6/5.75in) across all three sizes despite length varying 17-20in, and if taken as a 14cm depth the volume ratio blows out to 3.4x capacity (implausible for a slim frame bag - see MODEL-SPEC's 1.0-2.5x guideline), whereas reading it as the rear taper run (a dimension that plausibly stays similar across sizes sharing the same tail geometry) is physically consistent. Kept as a taper detail, not wid. Volume check with wid unverified: 43.2x5.7x10.8=2660cc=2.66L vs stated 1.9L, ratio 1.4 - normal.
